# Generated worker goldens

Each `<name>.cu` is the output of `cudamega.ProgramSource` for the fixture of
the same name in `golden_test.go`, written by

    go test -count=1 -run TestGoldenSourceMatchesGenerator ./x/cudamega/ -update-golden

`TestGoldenSourceMatchesGenerator` fails when the committed `.cu` and the
generator disagree, so the compiled artifacts below cannot silently become
evidence about source this package no longer emits.

There is one `.cu` per fixture and one `.ptx` per fixture per target. The
target is an input to the emitter now, but the text it emits does not depend
on it: `TestEmittedTextIsTargetInvariant` compiles every fixture for every
target and requires the bytes to be equal. What the target decides is which
programs the emitter will accept at all -- `cluster` scope needs `sm_90` --
and, downstream, what `ptxas` makes of the same source. So a second `.cu` per
target would be a second copy of one file, and the PTX is where the targets
actually differ.

The `.ptx`, `.cubin` and `.sass` are built from the committed `.cu` on the
authorized host. The `.cubin` is not committed: it is a build artifact of the
text files that are.

- host: `gpu-host` (192.0.2.1), NVIDIA GB10, compute capability 12.1,
  driver 580.173.02
- toolchain: `/usr/local/cuda-13.4/bin/nvcc`, release 13.4, V13.4.59;
  `cuobjdump` from the same toolkit
- PTX targets: `sm_80`, `sm_90`, `sm_121a`. `sm_80` is the floor the emitted
  primitives require: it is where `mbarrier` arrives, and
  `mbarrier.try_wait.parity.acquire.cta` was compiled for all three to
  establish that. `sm_90` is the floor `barrier.cluster` requires, which is
  why `cluster` scope is refused below it. `sm_121a` is the qualification
  host's arch-specific target; `sm_121` is the family and is not this target.
  `ptxas -arch=sm_121a` requires CUDA 12.9 or newer; the `nvcc` first on the
  host's `PATH` reports 12.0 and rejects it, so the full path above is not
  optional.
- SASS: `sm_121a` only. SASS is the encoding of one machine, and the only
  machine under authorization here is that one. `sm_80` and `sm_90` SASS would
  be a disassembly of a target nothing in this repository can run.
- date: 2026-09-22

Commands, per fixture and per PTX target:

    nvcc -arch=<target> -ptx <name>.cu -o <name>.<target>.ptx

and, on `sm_121a` only:

    nvcc -arch=sm_121a -cubin <name>.cu -o <name>.cubin
    cuobjdump -sass <name>.cubin > <name>.sm_121a.sass

The `sm_80` and `sm_90` PTX for a given fixture are byte-identical apart from
the `.target` line. That is a fact about CUDA 13.4 for these two programs, not
a guarantee; both are committed because the test asserts each file carries the
`.target` it is named for.

Provenance: the sources are generated by this package from fixtures defined in
this package. No vendor binary is redistributed here.

Nothing in this directory is evidence about runtime behavior. Compiling for a
target is not running on it. Both fixtures have since been launched on the host
above under recorded authorization, but that is a separate receipt in the lane
10 handoff -- these files are artifacts, not results.

## The dependency poll

The poll of a dependency's completion word is an acquiring load,

    asm volatile("ld.acquire.<scope>.u32 %0, [%1];" ...)

with `<scope>` one of `cta`, `gpu`, `sys` -- the scope the task declares.
Before S0.5 it was a `volatile` cast, which lowered to `ld.volatile.global`.
That is a real semantic change and not a rename: `volatile` suppresses
reordering by the compiler and says nothing at all about the hardware memory
model or about scope, so it never made the producer's writes visible to the
consumer. The acquire does. It is the reason every `.cu`, `.ptx` and `.sass`
in this directory was rebuilt for S0.5; nothing else in the emitted text
changed, and the `.cu` diff is confined to the poll body.

`artifact_test.go` reads the scope back out of the PTX: `pollRE` matches
`ld.acquire.(cta|gpu|sys).u32` and the test requires the scope on each poll to
be the one its task declares. `ld.acquire` is emitted by this primitive and by
nothing else in the worker, so matching it is narrower than matching
`ld.volatile` was.

Position is asserted only on `sm_121a` (`ptxPositional` in `artifact_test.go`).
CUDA 13.4 rotates the poll loop out of line on `sm_80` and `sm_90` and lays its
body down after the consumer's publication, so text order there is layout, not
execution order. The pre-S0.5 `sm_80` PTX, whose poll was the volatile load,
carries the same rotation -- this is the target's code generation and not
something the acquiring load introduced. Everything else (the publication
array, the poll offsets, the scopes, the synchronization census) is asserted on
all three targets.

`dag_worker`'s sixth parameter is 64 bits wide (`.param .u64` in the PTX). A
32-bit parameter takes epoch 2³² to zero, which the worker refuses as the
unpublished value; the native harness launches at that epoch so the width is
observable rather than asserted.

The `.ptx` and `.sass` also carry the in-kernel poll bound that makes a
dependency wait terminate: `setp.eq.b64` against 16777216 and a CAS installing
abort code 4 in PTX, `ISETP.NE.U64` against 0x1000000 and `ATOMG.E.CAS` in
SASS. `TestAbortCodesReachTheArtifact` and `TestSpinBoundSurvivesToSASS` assert
on them, so regenerating these files after changing `DefaultSpinLimit` or an
abort code requires updating those tests too.

## The mirrored text section

The CUDA 13.4 cubin built from `device-2cta.cu` carries two copies of every
text section: `.text.dag_worker` (0x2f00 bytes) and a compressed
`.nv.capmerc.text.dag_worker` (0x107c bytes), the second with its own
`.nv.merc.rela.text.dag_worker` relocations, `.nv.merc.symtab` and
`.nv.merc.nv.info*` tables. `cuobjdump -sass` disassembles the first. Nothing
here establishes which copy the driver executes, so `<name>.sass` is evidence
about `.text` and not about the mirror.
